decisions.argument_task: establish the shape of each numeric variable before any test assumes one

panels.title: sepal_length_cm is strongly left-skewed (median 5.80, IQR 5.10 to 6.40, n = 158)
petal_length_cm is moderately left-skewed (median 4.35, IQR 1.60 to 5.10, n = 158)
petal_width_cm is slightly left-skewed (median 1.30, IQR 0.30 to 1.80, n = 152)

decisions.uncertainty: median and interquartile range marked on every panel
decisions.title: 3 of 3 measured variables are skewed, so the analyses below summarise them by median rather than mean
decisions.caption: Distribution of each numeric variable, with the median and interquartile range marked. Panel order follows absolute skewness. Full box-and-whisker statistics are in Table 2.

body.fact: sepal_length_cm is strongly left-skewed (median 5.80, IQR 5.10 to 6.40, n = 158); petal_length_cm is moderately left-skewed (median 4.35, IQR 1.60 to 5.10, n = 158); petal_width_cm is slightly left-skewed (median 1.30, IQR 0.30 to 1.80, n = 152).
body.interpretation: Skewed variables are summarised by the median and IQR, and rank-based or Welch methods are preferred for them.
body.implication: These summaries, not the raw shape, should carry into any downstream model.

decisions.rationale: The shape of every numeric variable decides which test is legitimate later, so it is one argument and belongs in one figure. Splitting it across four would restate it four times.

rejected.chart_type: one histogram per variable as separate figures
rejected.reason: same argument repeated; the reader has to re-read the framing each time
understates the tail, which is precisely what decides the test choice

decisions.argument_task: test whether species moves the measured outcomes

panels.title: petal_length_cm differs across species (adjusted p = 3.697e-69)
panels.sentence: petal_length_cm differs across species by omega squared = 0.939 (95% CI 0.926 to 0.953), BH-adjusted p = 3.697e-69.

panels.title: petal_width_cm differs across species (adjusted p = 7.811e-65)
panels.sentence: petal_width_cm differs across species by omega squared = 0.926 (95% CI 0.910 to 0.943), BH-adjusted p = 7.811e-65.

panels.title: sepal_length_cm differs across species (adjusted p = 1.228e-23)
panels.sentence: sepal_length_cm differs across species by omega squared = 0.488 (95% CI 0.377 to 0.665), BH-adjusted p = 1.228e-23.

panels.title: sepal_width_cm differs across species (adjusted p = 9.266e-19)
panels.sentence: sepal_width_cm differs across species by omega squared = 0.418 (95% CI 0.304 to 0.537), BH-adjusted p = 9.266e-19.

decisions.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals on every group mean
decisions.title: 4 of 4 measured outcomes differ across species after correction for multiple comparisons
decisions.caption: Mean of each outcome by species with 95% confidence intervals, setosa, versicolor, virginica. Welch ANOVA (unequal variance); one-way ANOVA. Raw p values are BH-corrected across a family of 4 outcomes.

body.fact: petal_length_cm differs across species by omega squared = 0.939 (95% CI 0.926 to 0.953), BH-adjusted p = 3.697e-69; petal_width_cm differs across species by omega squared = 0.926 (95% CI 0.910 to 0.943), BH-adjusted p = 7.811e-65; sepal_length_cm differs across species by omega squared = 0.488 (95% CI 0.377 to 0.665), BH-adjusted p = 1.228e-23; sepal_width_cm differs across species by omega squared = 0.418 (95% CI 0.304 to 0.537), BH-adjusted p = 9.266e-19.
body.interpretation: Every tested outcome separates the groups.
body.implication: Carry the effect sizes forward, not the p values: a difference that is real can still be too small to matter.

decisions.rationale: One argument -- does the grouping variable move anything -- shown for every outcome at once. Four separate bar charts would be one argument told four times.

rejected.reason: group means are not parts of a whole
angle and area are hard to compare and imply the axes are commensurate

decisions.argument_task: show which measured variables move together, and which do not

panels.title: petal_length_cm and petal_width_cm are strongly associated (spearman = 0.94, p = 3.506e-70)
panels.sentence: petal_length_cm and petal_width_cm move together (spearman = 0.94, 95% CI 0.91 to 0.95, p = 3.506e-70, n = 152).

panels.title: sepal_length_cm and petal_length_cm are strongly associated (spearman = 0.88, p = 4.236e-53)
panels.sentence: sepal_length_cm and petal_length_cm move together (spearman = 0.88, 95% CI 0.84 to 0.91, p = 4.236e-53, n = 158).

decisions.uncertainty: LOWESS smoother with a bootstrap 95% band; Pearson r with a 95% CI
decisions.title: petal_length_cm and petal_width_cm are the strongest pair (spearman = 0.94)
decisions.caption: Each point is one observation. The line is a LOWESS smoother. Association only: this figure carries no direction of causation. Columns that restate the grouping variable are excluded.

body.fact: petal_length_cm and petal_width_cm move together (spearman = 0.94, 95% CI 0.91 to 0.95, p = 3.506e-70, n = 152); sepal_length_cm and petal_length_cm move together (spearman = 0.88, 95% CI 0.84 to 0.91, p = 4.236e-53, n = 158).
body.interpretation: A visible curve that a straight line would miss is the reason the smoother is drawn at all.
body.implication: Correlation here is a screening result. It says which relationships deserve a model, not which are real.

decisions.rationale: Scatter shows the shape of a relationship, which a coefficient cannot; a panel keeps the strongest pair and one contrast so the figure is not a correlation matrix in disguise.

rejected.reason: a third axis encodes nothing here
with this many columns it becomes a grid of numbers rather than an argument; the pairs that matter get their own panel

rules.one_argument_per_figure: panels, not repeats; a figure that cannot change the reader's understanding is not emitted
rules.uncertainty_mandatory: every estimate carries an interval, a band or a smoother
rules.title_is_the_finding: titles are computed from the numbers, never written by hand
rules.2d_before_3d: a third dimension must change the ranking, and needs a 2D fallback
rules.no_pie_for_comparison: pie and donut are excluded for >3 categories and for any time axis
rules.restatements_excluded: a column determined by the grouping variable is not evidence about it, and is kept out of both the figures and the family
